338647.title: The sharp snowflake exponent conjecture for modulus metrics on networks
338647.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected network, let $d_p$ denote its modulus metric for $p\in[1,\infty]$, and let $s(p)$ be the supremum of the exponents $t$ such that $d_p^t$ is a metric on every connected network. For the path graph $P_3$ on three nodes, the preceding calculation gives the upper bound $s(p)\leq p/(p-1)$ for $1<p<\infty$, with the endpoint values $s(1)=\infty$ and $s(\infty)=1$. **Sharp snowflake exponent conjecture.** For all $p\in[1,\infty]$, 

$$
s(p)=\frac{p}{p-1}.
$$

Namely, $P_3$ demonstrates the worst-case behavior. The conjecture asserts that the path graph gives the sharp obstruction to the triangle inequality for powers of modulus metrics. It has been answered in the affirmative using the theory of Fulkerson duality for modulus.

338672.title: Difference-product and difference-quotient sum-product conjectures
338672.literal_statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}$ be finite, and define

$$
A-A=\{a-b:a,b\in A\},\qquad AA^{-1}=\{ab^{-1}:a,b\in A\},
$$

with the convention $0^{-1}=0$. Also let $AA=\{ab:a,b\in A\}$. **Difference-product and difference-quotient conjecture.** For every fixed $\delta\leq 1$, one has both

$$
|A-A|+|AA^{-1}|\gtrsim |A|^{1+\delta},
$$

and

$$
|A-A|+|AA|\gtrsim |A|^{1+\delta}.
$$

These are sum-product-type expansion claims involving differences together with quotients or products. The candidate is presented without a name or resolution evidence, so its status remains open.

339053.title: Triangle condition conjecture for nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs
339053.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected, locally finite, nonamenable, quasi-transitive graph. For vertices $u,v\in V$, let $\tau_p(u,v)$ be the probability that $u$ and $v$ are connected in $G[p]$. Define the **triangle diagram** by

$$
\nabla_p=\sup_{v\in V}\sum_{x,y\in V}\tau_p(v,x)\tau_p(x,y)\tau_p(y,v).
$$

The **triangle condition** is the condition $\nabla_{p_c}<\infty$.

**Triangle condition conjecture.** One has $\nabla_{p_c}<\infty$.

The triangle condition is a sufficient condition for mean-field critical behaviour and is known in several settings, including high-dimensional Euclidean lattices. Whether it holds for every nonamenable quasi-transitive graph remains open.
339053.reason: Source hyperbolic theorem is not all nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs.
339053.precise_gap_or_bridge: Need summable triple two-point kernel at criticality without hyperbolicity. pc<pu or mean-field special cases do not give the universal triangle diagram.

339144.literal_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a prime with $p>2n$, and partition the reduced residues modulo $p$ into residue classes $I_i$ modulo $n$. Excluding $f(x)=\pm x\pmod p$, there are only finitely many Type (iia) examples. The conjecture formalizes the observed sparsity of these mappings beyond the trivial examples; the supplied text does not state a resolution.

339265.title: The universal deviation inequality for good drawings of complete graphs
339265.literal_statement:

**Universal deviation inequality.** For every face $F\in\mathcal{F}(D)$,

$$
\hat{\Delta}_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor-2}(D)\geq \bar{\Delta}_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor-2}(D).
$$

339820.literal_statement:

$$
\pi\sim\tau\quad\text{if and only if}\quad \pi\overset{s}{\sim}\tau.
$$

This conjecture asks whether ordinary Wilf-equivalence and strong c-Wilf equivalence coincide. The source notes that the analogous statement for ordinary Wilf-equivalence is already false for patterns of length $3$, and says that this conjecture appears to evade the methods developed in the paper.

340107.title: Submultiplicativity conjecture for the primitive-set ratio function
340107.literal_statement:
For $k>1$, let $Q(k)$ be the number of primitive subsets of $\\{1,2,\ldots,k\\}$ and define

$$
g(1)=1,\qquad g(k)=\frac{Q(k)}{Q(k-1)}-1.
$$

Thus $g(k)$ is the ratio of primitive subsets of $\\{1,2,\ldots,k\\}$ that contain $k$ to those that do not. **Submultiplicativity conjecture for $g$.** The function $g$ is submultiplicative in the following sense: if $(n,m)=1$, then

$$
g(nm)\leq g(n)g(m),
$$

and, for every prime $p$,

$$
g(p^{i+1})\leq g(p^i).
$$

These inequalities are proposed as conjectural improved upper-bound tools for the exponential growth constant associated with counting primitive sets. The supplied text gives no resolution of this conjecture.

340545.title: DeMarco–Kahn upper tail conjecture for strictly balanced graphs and dense regimes
340545.literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a graph, let $m_H$ denote its appearance-threshold parameter, and let the DeMarco–Kahn upper tail conjecture be the assertion that the upper-tail estimate stated above holds. Moreover, for every fixed $\gamma>0$, it is true under the additional assumption

$$
p\geqslant n^{-1/m_H+\gamma}.
$$
